explanation.whyCorrect: By the third trimester the uterus has grown tremendously. Extrinsic compression of other structures by the uterus causes esophageal reflux, edema and venous congestion, producing hemorrhoids, lower extremity edema and varicosities.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Declining placental function is a post-term concern affecting the fetus, not maternal veins.
whyWrongByChoice.C: GDM is not the described cause of third-trimester venous congestion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Iron-deficiency anemia is common but does not cause hemorrhoids or varicosities.
whyWrongByChoice.E: beta-hCG levels off after the first trimester and is linked to nausea, not venous congestion.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman at 22 weeks' gestation undergoes ultrasound, which shows a cervical length of 18 mm. She has no contractions or bleeding. Which of the following does this finding most strongly indicate?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Expected physiologic change at this stage

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased risk of spontaneous preterm birth

choices.label: E
choices.text: Need for early GBS screening and treatment

explanation.summary: A short cervix (<25 mm before 24 weeks) indicates increased risk of spontaneous preterm birth.
explanation.whyCorrect: A short cervix, typically defined as a cervical length under 25 mm before 24 weeks of gestation, may indicate an increased risk of spontaneous preterm birth and prompts closer surveillance or intervention.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Fetal lung maturity is not typically complete until about 36 weeks and is not assessed by cervical length.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A cervical length below 25 mm before 24 weeks is abnormal, not an expected change.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A short cervix points toward early, not prolonged, delivery.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GBS screening is done at 36 to 37 6/7 weeks; screening early is not recommended because colonization recurs.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman at 41 weeks' gestation reports decreased fetal movement. A biophysical profile is ordered to assess the fetus's risk of hypoxia. Which set of parameters does this evaluation combine?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Breathing movements, body movements, femur length, fluid volume, NST

choices.label: B
choices.text: Breathing movements, body movements, tone, abdominal girth, NST

choices.label: C
choices.text: Breathing movements, body movements, tone, fluid volume, maternal BP

choices.label: D
choices.text: Breathing movements, body movements, tone, fluid volume, NST

choices.label: E
choices.text: Head circumference, body movements, tone, fluid volume, NST

explanation.summary: BPP = fetal breathing, gross body movements, tone, amniotic fluid volume and NST reactivity.
explanation.whyCorrect: The biophysical profile combines fetal breathing movements, gross body movements, fetal tone, amniotic fluid volume and fetal heart rate reactivity on the nonstress test into a single scored evaluation that identifies fetuses at risk for hypoxia and guides surveillance or delivery decisions.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Femur length is a biometric measurement from the anatomy ultrasound, not a BPP component; fetal tone is.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Abdominal circumference is a biometric measurement, not a BPP component; amniotic fluid volume is.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Maternal blood pressure is monitored at prenatal visits but is not a BPP component; NST reactivity is.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Head circumference is a biometric measurement, not a BPP component; fetal breathing movements are.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman, gravida 1, at 9 weeks' gestation presents with vaginal bleeding and cramping. Transvaginal ultrasound shows an intrauterine embryo with no cardiac activity. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this pregnancy loss?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absent amniotic fluid from renal agenesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Structural weakness of the cervical tissue

explanation.summary: Chromosomal abnormalities are the most common cause of spontaneous abortion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Spontaneous abortion is loss of a pregnancy before 20 weeks. Chromosomal abnormalities are its most common cause, and their frequency rises with maternal age because oocytes, present since birth, accumulate mutations with aging.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Oligohydramnios from renal agenesis is a later-pregnancy problem, not the usual cause of early loss.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ultrasound shows an intrauterine embryo, so this is not an ectopic pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Placental abruption is typically a third-trimester complication, not a cause of 9-week loss.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cervical insufficiency causes painless dilation and second-trimester loss, not first-trimester embryonic demise.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman with a history of pelvic inflammatory disease has lower abdominal pain and a positive hCG test 7 weeks after her last menstrual period. Transvaginal ultrasound shows no intrauterine gestational sac. Which of the following is the most likely site of implantation?

explanation.summary: Most ectopic pregnancies implant in the ampulla of the uterine tube.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ampulla is the most common site of fertilization, and tubal scarring or adhesions there impede embryo transport, so it is the most common site of ectopic implantation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Abdominal implantation can occur but is far less common than tubal implantation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The ampulla, not the isthmus, is the most common tubal site.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The pouch of Douglas is a possible but uncommon ectopic site.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The tube (ampulla) is the most common location, not the ovary.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 6 weeks' gestation has mild pelvic pain. Blood pressure is 118/74 mm Hg and pulse is 80/min. Transvaginal ultrasound shows a small, intact gestation in the right uterine tube with no free fluid. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

explanation.summary: Stable patients with an unruptured ectopic pregnancy are preferentially treated with methotrexate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Methotrexate is preferred for a hemodynamically stable patient with an unruptured ectopic pregnancy; the tissue is then gradually absorbed or expelled. Surgery is reserved for rupture, significant hemorrhage, or instability.

whyWrongByChoice.A: D&C removes intrauterine tissue and cannot reach a tubal pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Surgery is required for rupture, hemorrhage, or instability, none of which is present.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Magnesium sulfate is used before 32 weeks in preterm labor for fetal neuroprotection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This regimen evacuates the uterus in spontaneous abortion; it does not treat a tubal gestation.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 31 weeks' gestation has regular uterine contractions, and her cervix is 4 cm dilated. She is given intramuscular betamethasone. Which of the following best describes how this drug benefits the newborn?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blocks calcium entry into myometrial smooth muscle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inhibits prostaglandin synthesis in the myometrium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Protects the neonatal brain against cerebral palsy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Relaxes uterine smooth muscle through beta-2 receptors

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stimulates surfactant release by type 2 alveolar cells

explanation.summary: Antenatal corticosteroids cross the placenta and accelerate fetal lung maturity by stimulating surfactant production.
explanation.whyCorrect: Betamethasone or dexamethasone crosses the placenta into the fetal circulation and stimulates type 2 alveolar cells to produce surfactant, reducing the severity of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome.

whyWrongByChoice.A: That is nifedipine's tocolytic mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: That is indomethacin's tocolytic mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Magnesium sulfate, not a corticosteroid, is given before 32 weeks to help prevent cerebral palsy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: That is terbutaline's tocolytic mechanism, not the corticosteroid's benefit.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman at 29 weeks' gestation is in preterm labor. She receives betamethasone and is also started on intravenous magnesium sulfate. Which of the following is the main purpose of the magnesium sulfate in this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accelerate surfactant production in the fetal lungs

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower the risk of cerebral palsy in the newborn

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prevent early closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reverse the cervical dilation already present

explanation.summary: Before 32 weeks, magnesium sulfate is given to help prevent cerebral palsy in the premature newborn.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cerebral palsy is a known complication of extreme prematurity. Magnesium sulfate given before 32 weeks helps prevent it, complementing corticosteroids, which address lung immaturity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: That is the role of the corticosteroid she already received.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Premature ductal closure is an NSAID adverse effect; magnesium is not given to prevent it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: No listed agent reverses cervical dilation; true labor may not be haltable.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Infection is treated with antibiotics; magnesium sulfate is given for neuroprotection.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 33 weeks' gestation has been receiving a tocolytic for several days for recurrent preterm contractions. Ultrasound now shows markedly reduced amniotic fluid, and fetal echocardiography shows narrowing of the ductus arteriosus. Which of the following agents is most likely responsible?

explanation.summary: NSAID tocolytics used for long periods or after 32 weeks can cause premature ductus closure and low amniotic fluid.
explanation.whyCorrect: Indomethacin decreases prostaglandin production. Because prostaglandins keep the ductus arteriosus open, prolonged use or use after 32 weeks can cause premature ductal closure and low amniotic fluid levels.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Betamethasone is a corticosteroid for fetal lung maturity, not a tocolytic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Magnesium sulfate is given before 32 weeks for fetal neuroprotection, not linked here to ductal closure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nifedipine, a calcium channel blocker, characteristically causes low blood pressure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Terbutaline's adverse effects are tachycardia and hyperglycemia.

questions.stem: A newborn delivered at 35 weeks has a flattened face, limb deformities, and severe respiratory difficulty. Prenatal ultrasound had shown almost no fluid around the fetus from early in the third trimester, with intact membranes. Which of the following fetal abnormalities most likely caused these findings?

explanation.summary: Oligohydramnios from absent fetal urine production causes compression deformities known as Potter sequence.
explanation.whyCorrect: Amniotic fluid is largely fetal urine. Renal agenesis prevents urine production, causing oligohydramnios, and longstanding compression produces the deformities of Potter sequence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anencephaly impairs swallowing and is associated with polyhydramnios.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A bilobed placenta is a cause of vasa previa, not of absent amniotic fluid.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Duodenal atresia prevents removal of fluid, producing polyhydramnios.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Impaired fetal swallowing causes polyhydramnios, not oligohydramnios.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 33 weeks' gestation has sudden bright red vaginal bleeding that began while she was resting. She has no pain or contractions. The uterus is soft and nontender, membranes are intact, and the fetal heart rate is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Painless third-trimester bleeding without warning is the classic presentation of placenta previa.
explanation.whyCorrect: Placenta previa, placental tissue over or near the cervical os, classically causes painless bleeding without warning after 20 weeks. Abruption instead causes painful bleeding with uterine tenderness.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cervical insufficiency presents with painless cervical dilation, not heavy bright red bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Abruption presents with pain, contractions, and uterine tenderness.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Preterm labor requires contractions with cervical change; she has no contractions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vasa previa bleeds at membrane rupture with fetal bradycardia; membranes are intact and heart rate normal.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman with chronic hypertension at 35 weeks' gestation presents with abdominal pain, dark vaginal bleeding, and a rigid, tender uterus. Two hours later, blood oozes from her intravenous sites and her platelet count is falling. Which of the following best explains the oozing?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Failure of the uterus to contract

explanation.summary: Complete placental abruption can be complicated by disseminated intravascular coagulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Painful bleeding with a tender uterus in a hypertensive patient indicates placental abruption. Disseminated intravascular coagulation can occur with complete abruption, producing diffuse bleeding such as oozing from IV sites.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Uterine atony causes postpartum hemorrhage, not diffuse coagulopathic oozing before delivery.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fetal-vessel bleeding (vasa previa) would not cause maternal IV-site oozing.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nifedipine causes low blood pressure, not a consumptive bleeding disorder.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Retained tissue after early pregnancy loss causes uterine bleeding or infection.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 39 weeks' gestation is in early labor. Her membranes rupture spontaneously, followed immediately by painless vaginal bleeding. The fetal heart rate abruptly falls to 80/min. Her vital signs are normal, and a prior ultrasound noted a velamentous cord insertion. Which of the following is the most likely source of the bleeding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cervical vessels torn during early dilation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Maternal decidual vessels behind a separated placenta

choices.label: C
choices.text: Maternal placental vessels overlying the os

choices.label: D
choices.text: Umbilical vessels running across the internal os

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uterine vessels from a ruptured uterine tube

explanation.summary: Vasa previa bleeding comes from exposed fetal vessels, so it causes fetal distress while the mother remains stable.
explanation.whyCorrect: In vasa previa, fetal vessels lie over the internal cervical os, often from a velamentous cord. Membrane rupture tears these vessels, causing painless bleeding that is fetal blood, hence the fetal bradycardia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cervical change does not explain fetal bradycardia right after rupture.
whyWrongByChoice.B: That is placental abruption, which is typically painful with uterine tenderness.
whyWrongByChoice.C: That is placenta previa, where bleeding is maternal and not triggered by membrane rupture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tubal rupture is an early ectopic pregnancy event, not a term labor finding.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman with a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy has an ultrasound at 22 weeks. One twin is small with signs of poor organ perfusion; the other is larger with cardiomegaly and signs of heart failure. Which of the following best explains the discordance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chromosomal abnormality affecting only the smaller twin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Separate placentas with unequal sites of implantation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Umbilical cord entanglement within a single amniotic sac

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unequal flow across placental vascular connections

explanation.summary: Twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome arises only in monochorionic twins from abnormal vascular connections in the shared placenta.
explanation.whyCorrect: In TTTS, abnormal connections within a single placenta create unequal blood flow: the donor twin develops growth restriction and hypoperfusion, and the recipient develops volume overload and heart failure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A karyotype problem would not explain heart failure in the larger co-twin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Maternal diabetes causes polyhydramnios, not donor-recipient discordance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Separate placentas describe dichorionic twins, which cannot develop TTTS.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cord entanglement complicates monoamniotic twins; these twins are diamniotic.

questions.stem: Ultrasound at 30 weeks' gestation shows an excess of amniotic fluid. After delivery, the newborn drools excessively, and a feeding tube cannot be passed into the stomach. Which of the following best explains the prenatal fluid abnormality?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Leakage through a defect in the amniotic sac

explanation.summary: Conditions that block fetal swallowing, such as esophageal atresia, cause polyhydramnios.
explanation.whyCorrect: The newborn has esophageal atresia. Because the fetus normally removes amniotic fluid by swallowing, obstruction of swallowing leaves excess fluid, producing polyhydramnios.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Maternal diabetes causes polyhydramnios by fetal polyuria, but this newborn has esophageal atresia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Obstructed urine flow reduces fluid, causing oligohydramnios.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Leakage reduces fluid, causing oligohydramnios.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Placental insufficiency causes growth restriction, not excess fluid.

questions.stem: A pregnancy loss is classified as a spontaneous abortion rather than a later fetal loss when the pregnancy fails to progress beyond which of the following gestational ages?

explanation.summary: Spontaneous abortion is a pregnancy that does not progress beyond 20 weeks' gestation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture defines spontaneous abortion as a pregnancy that does not progress beyond 20 weeks. The same 20-week boundary marks the start of the preterm labor window (20-37 weeks).

whyWrongByChoice.A: 12 weeks marks the end of the first trimester, not the spontaneous abortion cutoff.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The cutoff is 20 weeks, not 24.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 32 weeks is the threshold for magnesium sulfate and NSAID cautions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 37 weeks is the upper limit of preterm labor.

questions.stem: A 37-year-old woman who smokes half a pack of cigarettes daily and had one spontaneous abortion 2 years ago asks about her risk of another pregnancy loss. She had one uncomplicated vaginal delivery before that. Which of the following factors is most strongly associated with her risk?

explanation.summary: Advanced maternal age (35 or older) is the most significant risk factor for spontaneous abortion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Smoking, prior spontaneous abortion, and maternal age 35 or older are all risk factors, but maternal age is the most significant because aging oocytes are more likely to carry chromosomal abnormalities.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Smoking is a risk factor but less significant than maternal age.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Having given birth is not itself a risk; only grand multiparity carries added risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prior spontaneous abortion is a risk factor but less significant than maternal age.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A prior uncomplicated delivery is not a risk factor for spontaneous abortion.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman at 10 weeks' gestation has light vaginal bleeding for 2 days. Ultrasound shows an intrauterine embryo with cardiac activity. The bleeding stops, and she later delivers a healthy infant at term. Which of the following best describes her first-trimester event?

explanation.summary: A threatened abortion is first-trimester bleeding without loss of the pregnancy and carries a more favorable outcome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Threatened abortion refers to first-trimester bleeding in which the pregnancy is not lost. It is associated with a more favorable outcome than spontaneous abortion, as this pregnancy continued to term.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cervical insufficiency causes painless dilation and second-trimester loss.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The embryo is intrauterine, excluding ectopic implantation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Previa bleeding typically presents after 20 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Spontaneous abortion requires loss of the pregnancy before 20 weeks.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman at an estimated 8 weeks' gestation has vaginal bleeding and pelvic cramping. Pelvic examination and ultrasound are performed. Which of the following laboratory findings would most support early pregnancy loss?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Serum glucose that is markedly elevated

choices.label: B
choices.text: Serum hCG that is undetectable at baseline

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serum hCG that plateaus or declines

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum hCG that rises as expected

explanation.summary: In early pregnancy loss, serum hCG typically plateaus or declines.
explanation.whyCorrect: Evaluation of suspected spontaneous abortion includes pelvic examination, ultrasound (no embryo or no cardiac activity), and serial serum hCG, which typically plateaus or declines when the pregnancy is failing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glucose does not assess pregnancy viability.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An undetectable hCG would argue against pregnancy altogether.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An appropriately rising hCG argues for an ongoing pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A positive test only confirms pregnancy; it does not show loss.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman with a nonviable 8-week intrauterine pregnancy chooses medication to evacuate the uterus. She receives mifepristone, followed later by misoprostol. Which of the following describes the mechanism of the first drug?

explanation.summary: Mifepristone is a progesterone antagonist; misoprostol is a prostaglandin agonist.
explanation.whyCorrect: The most effective medication regimen to evacuate the uterus is mifepristone, a progesterone antagonist, followed by misoprostol, a prostaglandin agonist.

whyWrongByChoice.A: That is misoprostol, the second drug.
whyWrongByChoice.C: That is nifedipine, a tocolytic.
whyWrongByChoice.D: That is indomethacin, an NSAID tocolytic.
whyWrongByChoice.E: That is terbutaline, a tocolytic.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman conceives fraternal twins after two separate oocytes are fertilized. Which of the following placental arrangements is expected?

explanation.summary: All dizygotic twins are dichorionic diamniotic, with separate placentas and amniotic sacs.
explanation.whyCorrect: All dizygotic twins, and some monozygotic twins, are dichorionic diamniotic. Shared placentas, shared sacs, or shared body parts occur only in monozygotic twins, depending on when embryonic division occurs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Conjoined twins are a rare monozygotic outcome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Twins with separate placentas each have their own sac.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A shared placenta occurs only in some monozygotic twins.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A shared placenta and sac occurs only in some monozygotic twins.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman with a nonviable first-trimester pregnancy is weighing mifepristone plus misoprostol against dilation and curettage. Which of the following is a disadvantage of the medication approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Expulsion occurs away from clinical care

choices.label: B
choices.text: It carries the usual risks of surgery

choices.label: E
choices.text: It uses suction through a curette

explanation.summary: With medication evacuation, expulsion happens outside the clinical setting, so complications are addressed later.
explanation.whyCorrect: Mifepristone followed by misoprostol is the most effective medication to evacuate the uterus, but expulsion occurs outside the clinical setting, delaying management of complications such as heavy bleeding. D&C carries the usual surgical risks instead.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Surgical risks apply to dilation and curettage, not the medication approach.
whyWrongByChoice.C: It is used for early pregnancy loss, which by definition is before 20 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mechanical dilation is part of D&C.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Suction through a curette is the D&C technique.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman with a history of a sexually transmitted infection treated 3 years ago is diagnosed with a tubal ectopic pregnancy. Which of the following most directly explains her increased risk?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chromosomal errors arising in aging oocytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess amniotic fluid distending the uterus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Placental implantation near the internal cervical os

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scarring that impedes transport of the embryo

choices.label: E
choices.text: Structural weakness of the cervical tissue

explanation.summary: Acquired tubal adhesions, typically from STI-related inflammation, impede embryo transport and cause ectopic implantation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Abnormal reproductive anatomy is the most significant ectopic risk factor. Inflammation from a sexually transmitted infection causes tubal adhesions that impede embryo transport, so the blastocyst implants in the tube.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Oocyte aging drives spontaneous abortion risk, not tubal implantation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Polyhydramnios is a later-pregnancy condition unrelated to tubal implantation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: That describes placenta previa, an intrauterine implantation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cervical insufficiency causes second-trimester loss, not ectopic pregnancy.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain. Appendicitis is suspected. Her last menstrual period was 7 weeks ago. Which of the following should be done first to evaluate for an important alternative diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Ectopic pregnancy must be in the differential of any reproductive-age woman with severe abdominal pain; hCG confirms pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: When a reproductive-age woman has severe abdominal pain, ectopic pregnancy must always be considered alongside appendicitis. An hCG test confirms pregnancy, and transvaginal ultrasound then attempts to locate the embryo.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The amniotic fluid index evaluates fluid volume later in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cervical length screening addresses cervical insufficiency, not acute pain.
whyWrongByChoice.C: D&C is a treatment for intrauterine pregnancy loss, not an initial test.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Treatment is not given before pregnancy and its location are established.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman with a known right tubal ectopic pregnancy develops sudden severe abdominal pain. Blood pressure is 78/44 mm Hg and pulse is 132/min. Ultrasound shows a large amount of free fluid in the pelvis. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

explanation.summary: Rupture, significant hemorrhage, or hemodynamic instability requires surgery.
explanation.whyCorrect: She has a ruptured ectopic pregnancy with hemorrhage and hemodynamic instability. Methotrexate is only for stable patients with unruptured ectopic pregnancy; surgery is required here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: D&C cannot reach a tubal pregnancy or control intra-abdominal bleeding.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Untreated ruptured ectopic pregnancy can cause fatal hemorrhage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Methotrexate is reserved for stable patients with unruptured ectopic pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This regimen evacuates the uterus and does not address tubal rupture.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman has an untreated ectopic pregnancy in the uterine tube. Which of the following best explains why the uterine tube is prone to rupture as the pregnancy advances?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amniotic fluid accumulating behind a blocked tube

choices.label: B
choices.text: An invasive blastocyst enlarging in a narrow tube

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rising progesterone thinning the tubal muscle

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tubal contractions squeezing against the embryo

explanation.summary: The blastocyst is highly invasive, and the small uterine tube ruptures as the embryo and placenta enlarge.
explanation.whyCorrect: The blastocyst adheres to and invades wherever it attaches. Because the uterine tube is small, it cannot accommodate the growing embryo and placenta, so it tends to rupture, risking fatal hemorrhage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amniotic fluid accumulation is not the mechanism of tubal rupture.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypertension is linked to placental abruption, not tubal rupture.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The lecture attributes rupture to invasion and tubal size, not a hormonal effect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rupture results from growth within a small tube, not tubal contraction.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 32 weeks' gestation reports cramping, low back pain, and increased vaginal discharge. Which of the following findings establishes the diagnosis of preterm labor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cramping with back pain and discharge alone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Low amniotic fluid index on ultrasound

choices.label: C
choices.text: Membrane rupture before the onset of labor

explanation.summary: Preterm labor is diagnosed clinically by uterine contractions with cervical dilation between 20 and 37 weeks.
explanation.whyCorrect: Very premature labor may present subtly with cramping, back pain, and discharge, but the diagnosis requires uterine contractions accompanied by cervical dilation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: These subtle symptoms prompt evaluation but do not establish the diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A low index indicates oligohydramnios, not labor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: That describes PPROM, a separate cause of preterm birth.
whyWrongByChoice.D: That describes cervical insufficiency.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman at 21 weeks' gestation is found on routine examination to have a shortened, dilated cervix. She has no pain, no bleeding, and tocodynamometry shows no contractions. Membranes are intact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: Cervical insufficiency presents with painless cervical shortening and dilation in the absence of contractions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cervical insufficiency results from structural weakness of the cervix and causes painless shortening and dilation without contractions. It raises the risk of PPROM, second-trimester loss, and preterm birth.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Abruption presents with painful bleeding and uterine tenderness.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Preterm labor requires contractions that cause cervical change.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Her membranes are intact.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Threatened abortion is first-trimester bleeding without loss.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 33 weeks' gestation notices a sudden gush of clear fluid from the vagina. She has no contractions, and examination confirms leaking amniotic fluid. Which of the following best describes this condition?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vasa previa with fetal vessel rupture

explanation.summary: PPROM is rupture of the fetal membranes before labor and before 37 weeks.
explanation.whyCorrect: Preterm premature rupture of membranes is rupture of the fetal membranes before labor begins and before 37 weeks' gestation. It is one of the processes, with preterm labor and cervical insufficiency, that lead to preterm birth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cervical insufficiency is painless dilation from cervical weakness, not fluid leakage.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Polyhydramnios is an excess of fluid, not its leakage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Preterm labor requires contractions with cervical dilation, and she has no contractions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vasa previa presents with bleeding at membrane rupture and fetal bradycardia.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman without diabetes at 30 weeks' gestation is treated with terbutaline for preterm contractions and receives no other medications. The next day her pulse is 118/min and her plasma glucose is 205 mg/dL. Which of the following best explains the hyperglycemia?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased intestinal absorption of dietary glucose

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reduced insulin release from calcium channel blockade

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduced renal excretion of filtered glucose

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suppressed insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells

explanation.summary: Beta-2 agonist tocolytics cause hyperglycemia by stimulating hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Terbutaline's beta-2 stimulation relaxes the uterus but also drives hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis. Although it increases insulin release, reduced insulin sensitivity further contributes to hyperglycemia; cardiac stimulation explains the tachycardia.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Terbutaline's hyperglycemia is hepatic in origin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: She received no calcium channel blocker.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Renal handling is not the mechanism described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Beta-2 agonists increase, not suppress, insulin release.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 30 weeks' gestation in preterm labor is given a tocolytic that blocks L-type calcium channels in uterine smooth muscle. Which of the following adverse effects is most characteristic of this drug?

explanation.summary: Calcium channel blocker tocolytics such as nifedipine can cause low blood pressure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nifedipine, a calcium channel blocker, relaxes uterine smooth muscle and can cause low blood pressure as a side effect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: That is the intended effect of corticosteroids.
whyWrongByChoice.B: That is a beta-2 agonist (terbutaline) effect.
whyWrongByChoice.D: That is an NSAID (indomethacin) effect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Low amniotic fluid is an NSAID effect.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 32 weeks' gestation has a fundal height 5 cm less than expected for her dates. Her physician suspects a deficiency of the fluid surrounding the fetus. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to confirm this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amniocentesis with karyotype analysis of the fluid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cervical length measurement by transvaginal ultrasound

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serial measurement of serum hCG concentration

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ultrasound measurement of the amniotic fluid index

explanation.summary: Oligohydramnios is confirmed with the ultrasonographic amniotic fluid index compared with gestational-age norms.
explanation.whyCorrect: A fundal height less than expected raises suspicion of oligohydramnios. Ultrasound determines the amniotic fluid index, an estimate of fluid volume that is compared with reference standards for gestational age.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amniocentesis does not measure fluid volume.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cervical length screens for cervical insufficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.C: hCG trends evaluate early pregnancy viability.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Monitoring contractions evaluates labor, not fluid volume.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 34 weeks' gestation has a low amniotic fluid index. Ultrasound shows normal-appearing fetal kidneys and a normally filling fetal bladder. She reports intermittent watery discharge over the past week. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her oligohydramnios?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bilateral agenesis of the fetal kidneys

choices.label: D
choices.text: Leakage of fluid through ruptured membranes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Obstruction of the fetal urinary outflow tract

explanation.summary: Oligohydramnios arises from reduced fetal urine production or loss of fluid through a ruptured or defective amniotic sac.
explanation.whyCorrect: The two major categories of oligohydramnios are reduced fetal urine production and loss of fluid from rupture or a defect in the sac. Normal kidneys and bladder filling with watery discharge point to leakage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fetal kidneys are present and the bladder fills normally.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fetal polyuria causes polyhydramnios.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Impaired swallowing causes polyhydramnios.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Obstruction would show an abnormal urinary tract or bladder.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with poorly controlled pregestational diabetes mellitus is found at 31 weeks to have an excess of amniotic fluid. The fetal anatomy survey is normal. Which of the following best explains the fluid abnormality?

explanation.summary: Maternal diabetes is commonly associated with polyhydramnios through fetal polyuria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Polyhydramnios is commonly associated with maternal diabetes mellitus, in which fetal polyuria contributes to increased amniotic fluid volume. The normal anatomy argues against a swallowing defect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Leakage decreases fluid, causing oligohydramnios.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Urinary obstruction causes oligohydramnios.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Swallowing defects such as atresia would appear on the anatomy survey.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Placental insufficiency causes growth restriction.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman whose pregnancy was complicated by marked polyhydramnios from fetal duodenal atresia delivers vaginally at 38 weeks. She took no medications during pregnancy. Which of the following maternal complications is she at greatest risk for in the hour after delivery?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bleeding from a ruptured uterine tube

explanation.summary: Uterine overdistension from polyhydramnios raises the risk of postpartum hemorrhage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Polyhydramnios overdistends the uterus, increasing the risk of postpartum hemorrhage along with preterm labor, malpresentation, abruption, and cord prolapse.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tubal rupture is a complication of early ectopic pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: She received no terbutaline.
whyWrongByChoice.D: She received no calcium channel blocker.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cervical insufficiency is a second-trimester problem, not a postpartum one.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman at 30 weeks' gestation has painless vaginal bleeding, and transvaginal ultrasound shows placental tissue over the internal cervical os. Which of the following in her history most increased her risk for this condition?

explanation.summary: Risk factors for placenta previa include prior previa, prior cesarean delivery, and multiple gestation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cause of placenta previa is unknown, but prior placenta previa, prior cesarean delivery, and multiple gestation increase its incidence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Maternal hypertension is a leading cause of placental abruption.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Maternal diabetes is associated with polyhydramnios.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tubal infection and adhesions increase ectopic pregnancy risk.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Blunt trauma is a leading cause of placental abruption.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman at 18 weeks' gestation has no symptoms. A routine anatomy ultrasound shows the placental edge partially covering the internal cervical os. Which of the following is the most accurate counseling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It requires cesarean delivery at 20 weeks

choices.label: C
choices.text: It usually persists and requires cesarean

choices.label: D
choices.text: It usually progresses to placental abruption

choices.label: E
choices.text: It usually resolves as the uterus elongates

explanation.summary: About 90% of previas found at 16-20 weeks resolve through uterine elongation or regression of the placental edge.
explanation.whyCorrect: Placenta previa found on routine ultrasound between 16 and 20 weeks resolves in about 90% of cases, from uterine elongation or regression of the placental edge. Persistent previa is then managed with cesarean delivery at term.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Asymptomatic previa is delivered by cesarean at term, not at 20 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tocolytics treat preterm contractions, not asymptomatic previa.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Most early previas resolve on their own.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Previa and abruption are distinct conditions.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman, para 6, has heavy bleeding immediately after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery of a healthy infant. The placenta delivered intact, and the uterus feels soft and poorly contracted. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her bleeding?

explanation.summary: Grand multiparity (five or more prior births) increases the risk of uterine atony and postpartum hemorrhage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Multiparity alone is not a risk, but grand multiparity is associated with preterm labor, postpartum hemorrhage, placenta previa, and uterine atony, the failure of the uterus to contract sufficiently during and after childbirth.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cervical insufficiency causes painless second-trimester dilation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Abruption is separation before delivery; the placenta delivered intact after an uncomplicated birth.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ectopic pregnancy is an early pregnancy complication.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vasa previa causes fetal bleeding at membrane rupture, not postpartum maternal hemorrhage.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman with a singleton pregnancy has an ultrasound at 32 weeks showing an estimated fetal weight below the 10th percentile. She is normotensive, does not smoke or have diabetes, and fetal karyotype is normal. Which of the following is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Fetal growth restriction is most commonly caused by placental insufficiency.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fetal growth restriction (EFW or abdominal circumference below the 10th percentile) is most often caused by placental insufficiency restricting oxygen and nutrient delivery. Maternal, chromosomal, and multiple-gestation causes are excluded by the stem.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The fetal karyotype is normal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Renal agenesis causes oligohydramnios and Potter sequence.
whyWrongByChoice.C: She does not have diabetes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TTTS occurs only in monochorionic twins; this is a singleton.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 17 weeks' gestation, dated by a first-trimester ultrasound, requests termination of pregnancy. She has no medical conditions and no prior uterine surgery. Which of the following is the most appropriate method at this gestational age?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mifepristone given as a single agent

choices.label: E
choices.text: Misoprostol given as a single agent

explanation.summary: Dilation and evacuation is the method used for abortion beyond the first trimester, up to 24 weeks.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture's timing table limits medical abortion to about 10 weeks (FDA) or 12 weeks (WHO) and manual vacuum aspiration to 10-14 weeks. Dilation and evacuation, which uses cervical dilation plus instruments and suction to empty the uterus, can be performed up to 24 weeks, making it the appropriate choice at 17 weeks.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Manual vacuum aspiration is used up to about 10-14 weeks, so 17 weeks is beyond its range.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The combined medical regimen is used up to 10 weeks (FDA) or 12 weeks (WHO).
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mifepristone is used in combination with misoprostol in early pregnancy, not alone in the second trimester.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Misoprostol alone is a first-trimester option (up to 10 weeks) when mifepristone is unavailable.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman at 6 weeks' gestation chooses medical abortion and takes mifepristone in the clinic, with a second medication to be taken at home. Which of the following is the mechanism of action of the drug taken in the clinic?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blocks estrogen receptors in the endometrium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blocks progesterone needed to sustain the pregnancy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibits folate metabolism in the trophoblast

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stimulates uterine smooth muscle to contract

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suppresses pituitary release of luteinizing hormone

explanation.summary: Mifepristone blocks the progesterone that supports the conceptus during pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Per the lecture's table, mifepristone blocks the progesterone needed to support the conceptus during pregnancy. It is used up to 10 weeks in combination with misoprostol, which then causes uterine contractions that expel the conceptus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mifepristone acts on progesterone, not estrogen, signaling.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The lecture does not describe an antifolate mechanism for either abortion medication.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inducing uterine contractions to expel the conceptus is the action of misoprostol, the second drug.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mifepristone does not act by suppressing pituitary gonadotropins.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman at 8 weeks' gestation elects medical abortion. The clinic where she is seen has no supply of mifepristone. Which of the following regimens is most appropriate?

explanation.summary: When mifepristone is unavailable, misoprostol can be used alone for medical abortion up to 10 weeks.
explanation.whyCorrect: Medical abortion uses mifepristone plus misoprostol, but the lecture notes that misoprostol can be used alone when mifepristone is not available. At 8 weeks she is within the medical-abortion window, and misoprostol causes uterine contractions that expel the conceptus.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Uterotonics like this are used for bleeding; the lecture's alternative regimen is misoprostol alone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Oxytocin is not described as a medical abortion regimen in early pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Progesterone supports the conceptus; blocking it (not giving it) is the goal of mifepristone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antifibrinolytics are used to treat hemorrhage, not to induce abortion.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman took mifepristone and then misoprostol at 8 weeks' gestation 5 days ago. For the past 3 hours she has soaked more than one pad per hour, with cramping. Blood pressure is 112/70 mm Hg and pulse is 98/min. After assessing her hemodynamic status, which of the following evaluations is most important?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abdominal CT to look for bowel injury

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blood cultures for suspected septic endometritis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ultrasound for retained products of conception

explanation.summary: Hemorrhage after medical abortion should prompt evaluation for incomplete abortion (retained products of conception).
explanation.whyCorrect: Filling a pad an hour warrants contact and evaluation. The lecture states that hemorrhage after a medical abortion should prompt evaluation for incomplete abortion or retained products of conception, along with possible evaluation for an underlying bleeding disorder.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Visceral injury is a concern with surgical perforation, not medical abortion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: She has no fever, discharge, or other signs of infection; bleeding is the problem.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tubal patency is irrelevant to acute bleeding after abortion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Uterine perforation is a rare complication of surgical, not medical, abortion.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman underwent vacuum aspiration at 9 weeks' gestation 4 days ago. She now has a temperature of 38.6 C (101.5 F), lower abdominal pain, uterine tenderness, and a foul-smelling cervical discharge. Leukocyte count is 16,000/mm3. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis and appropriate management?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Uterine atony treated with uterotonic drugs

explanation.summary: Fever, pelvic pain, leukocytosis, and foul discharge after surgical abortion indicate endometritis requiring antibiotics.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture lists fever, abdominal or pelvic pain, leukocytosis, and foul-smelling vaginal or cervical discharge as the signs of infection (endometritis) after surgical abortion. Patients with infection require antibiotic treatment, and severe infection may require hospitalization. Infection is uncommon (<1%) when prophylaxis is used.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Fever, leukocytosis, and foul discharge are not expected post-procedure findings.
whyWrongByChoice.C: She had a surgical procedure, and misoprostol fever is low-grade without other symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Atony causes hemorrhage, not fever with foul discharge.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Perforation presents with concern for hemorrhage or organ injury, not purulent discharge with leukocytosis.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 20-year-old woman at 6 weeks' gestation chooses medical abortion with mifepristone and misoprostol. She asks which antibiotic she should take beforehand to prevent infection. According to ACOG, which of the following is the most appropriate response?

explanation.summary: ACOG does not recommend antibiotic prophylaxis before medical abortion.
explanation.whyCorrect: According to ACOG, antibiotics are not necessary before medical abortion. By contrast, ACOG and WHO recommend antibiotic prophylaxis (doxycycline, azithromycin, or metronidazole) for surgical abortion, alongside sterile technique.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Azithromycin is used for surgical abortion prophylaxis, not medical abortion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: No antibiotic prophylaxis is recommended for medical abortion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxycycline is a prophylactic option for surgical abortion, not medical abortion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metronidazole is a surgical prophylaxis option; medical abortion does not require antibiotics.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman has an uncomplicated vacuum aspiration at 8 weeks' gestation. She wants a hormonal implant to prevent future pregnancy and has no contraindications. When is the most appropriate time to place the implant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: After 3 months of using condoms alone

choices.label: B
choices.text: After a negative pregnancy test in 4 weeks

choices.label: C
choices.text: After her first menstrual period returns

choices.label: E
choices.text: Immediately, at the time of the abortion

explanation.summary: Most contraceptive methods, including implants, can be started immediately after abortion if medically eligible and desired.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that most contraceptive methods after abortion should be initiated immediately if the patient is medically eligible and it aligns with her goals, including hormonal implants, oral contraceptives, IUDs, condoms, emergency contraception, and cervical caps.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No waiting period is recommended before starting a hormonal method.
whyWrongByChoice.B: There is no need to delay contraception for a confirmatory test in an eligible patient.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Waiting for menses is unnecessary; most methods can start immediately if eligible.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Routine in-person follow-up is not required, and delay leaves her unprotected.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: Before performing a surgical abortion, a physician explains to the patient how the procedure is done and its risks. To complete the informed consent process, which of the following must also be discussed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Her detailed reasons for seeking abortion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Her partner's written agreement to proceed

choices.label: D
choices.text: The physician's personal views on abortion

choices.label: E
choices.text: The worldwide legal status of abortion

explanation.summary: Informed consent covers how the procedure is done, its risks, its benefits, and the available alternatives.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that obtaining informed consent involves educating patients on how the procedure is done, its risks and benefits, and available alternatives, so that the patient fully understands the procedure before giving permission.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Patients do not have to justify their decision to give informed consent.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Consent is the patient's own decision; a partner's agreement is not an element.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Counseling should be nonjudgmental; personal views are not part of consent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Global legal status is not an element of informed consent for her procedure.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman at 7 weeks' gestation is deciding whether to continue her pregnancy. She asks how the risk of death from abortion compares with the risk of death from continuing a pregnancy. According to CDC data, which of the following statements is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Abortion carries far lower risk, constant across gestation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Abortion carries far lower risk, rising with gestational age

choices.label: C
choices.text: Abortion carries higher risk, falling with gestational age

choices.label: D
choices.text: Continued pregnancy carries lower risk before 12 weeks

choices.label: E
choices.text: The two carry similar risk, about 1 per 100,000 each

explanation.summary: Abortion mortality (0.3-1 per 100,000) is far lower than that of continued pregnancy (17.9 per 100,000) and rises with gestational age.
explanation.whyCorrect: Per the CDC figures in the lecture, the risk of death from abortion is 0.3-1 per 100,000, increasing with gestational age, whereas the risk of death from a continued pregnancy is 17.9 per 100,000. Rates vary by geography, age, race and ethnicity, and underlying medical conditions.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lecture states abortion mortality increases with increasing gestational age.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Abortion mortality (0.3-1/100,000) is far below that of continued pregnancy (17.9/100,000) and rises with gestation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Abortion is safer than continued pregnancy; there is no early-gestation reversal.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Continued pregnancy carries about 17.9 deaths per 100,000, far higher than abortion.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A public health team compares countries that have highly restrictive abortion laws with countries that provide broad legal access. Which of the following outcomes is most consistently observed in the countries with highly restrictive laws?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A higher proportion of unsafe abortions

choices.label: B
choices.text: A lower rate of abortion-related hemorrhage

explanation.summary: Highly restrictive abortion laws are associated with a significantly higher proportion of unsafe abortions.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture notes that patients usually find a way to induce an abortion whether or not it is legal, and that in countries with highly restrictive laws the proportion of unsafe abortions is significantly higher, endangering patients' health and lives.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Unsafe abortion raises, not lowers, the risk of hemorrhage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Restriction does not stop patients from seeking to end pregnancies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sepsis is a serious complication of unsafe abortion, which is more common under restriction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Evidence suggests patients usually find a way to induce abortion whether or not it is legal.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A physician is counseling a 19-year-old woman at 6 weeks' gestation who has decided to have an abortion. Which of the following statements by the physician best reflects recommended counseling practice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: "Before we proceed, let me share my own opinion."

choices.label: B
choices.text: "Have you thought about how your family will react?"

choices.label: C
choices.text: "I understand this is an unwanted pregnancy for you."

choices.label: D
choices.text: "Let's go over each option and what to expect with it."

choices.label: E
choices.text: "Since this pregnancy was unplanned, let's review options."

explanation.summary: Abortion counseling should use clear, objective, noninflammatory language that avoids labels such as 'unplanned' or 'unwanted.'
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture's counseling guidelines are to avoid judgment, provide clear accurate information, use noninflammatory language (avoiding qualifiers like 'unplanned' or 'unwanted'), provide resources, and create a safe space. Offering to review each option and what to expect does this.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clinicians should avoid judgment and maintain objectivity to respect autonomy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: This question implies judgment rather than objective, supportive counseling.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Calling the pregnancy 'unwanted' is inflammatory language the lecture advises against.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Qualifiers such as 'unplanned' should be avoided when describing the pregnancy.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman at 7 weeks' gestation takes mifepristone and, 1 day later, misoprostol. Six hours after the misoprostol dose, her temperature is 37.9 C (100.2 F). She has cramping similar to menses, no uterine tenderness, and no abnormal discharge. Leukocyte count is normal. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for her temperature?

explanation.summary: Up to half of patients given misoprostol have a low-grade fever without other symptoms; infection after medical abortion is rare.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture notes that infection after medical abortion is rare, although half of patients given misoprostol may have low-grade fevers without other symptoms. Her isolated low-grade fever with normal leukocyte count and no tenderness or discharge fits this expected drug effect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lecture attributes post-medication low-grade fever to misoprostol, not mifepristone.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sepsis would not present as an isolated low-grade temperature with normal labs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Endometritis would bring pelvic tenderness, leukocytosis, or foul discharge, all absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Perforation is a complication of surgical abortion, not medical abortion.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 9 weeks' gestation develops cramping and passes tissue at home. She has taken no medications and had no procedures. Ultrasound shows an empty uterus. Which of the following terms best describes this event?

explanation.summary: Spontaneous abortion (miscarriage, pregnancy loss) occurs without medical or surgical intervention.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture defines spontaneous abortion as pregnancy termination that occurs without medical or surgical intervention, often without obvious reasons; in lay terms it is called pregnancy loss or miscarriage. Induced abortion, by contrast, uses medical or surgical management.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The uterus is empty, so no products of conception are retained.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Induced abortion is performed using medical or surgical management; none occurred here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Self-management involves taking medications to terminate pregnancy, which she did not do.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Unsafe abortion refers to a termination by an unskilled person or in a substandard environment.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 7 weeks' gestation obtains quality-assured mifepristone and misoprostol, receives accurate instructions on their use, and completes her abortion at home without complications. According to the WHO definition, how is this abortion best classified?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Incomplete, because no aspiration was performed

choices.label: B
choices.text: Safe, as it was self-managed with correct information

choices.label: C
choices.text: Spontaneous, because no procedure was performed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Unsafe, because it took place outside a medical facility

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unsafe, because no clinician was physically present

explanation.summary: WHO considers abortion safe when an appropriate method is used by a skilled person or safely self-managed with correct information and quality medications.
explanation.whyCorrect: WHO defines safe abortion as termination using a recommended method appropriate for the duration of pregnancy, performed by a person with the necessary skills, or safely self-managed with correct information and quality medications. This patient meets the self-managed criterion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspiration is not required; nothing suggests retained tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Taking medications to end a pregnancy is induced, not spontaneous, abortion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Location outside a facility does not make an informed self-managed abortion unsafe.
whyWrongByChoice.E: WHO counts self-management with correct information and quality medications as safe.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A physician notes that a patient's options for managing her pregnancy have been shaped by her lack of insurance, the long distance to the nearest clinic, and her state's laws. Which of the following concepts most directly describes how these social, economic, and political forces affect her reproductive decisions?

explanation.summary: Reproductive justice acknowledges the social, economic, and political influences on a patient's ability to make reproductive decisions.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture distinguishes reproductive autonomy (the individual's right to decide and control contraception, pregnancy, and childbearing) from reproductive justice, which acknowledges the social, economic, and political influences on patients' ability to make healthy decisions about their bodies, sexuality, and reproduction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Beneficence is the duty to act in the patient's interest, not the influence of social forces.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Informed consent covers understanding a procedure's details, risks, benefits, and alternatives.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nonmaleficence is the duty to avoid harm, not a framework for structural influences.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Autonomy is the individual's right to decide and control contraception, pregnancy, and childbearing.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman decided at 6 weeks' gestation to have an abortion. The nearest provider is 300 miles away, she has no car, and she cannot afford unpaid time off work. She is finally able to reach the clinic at 13 weeks. Which of the following best describes the consequence of these barriers?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A higher lifetime risk of major depression

choices.label: B
choices.text: A higher risk of misoprostol-induced fever

choices.label: C
choices.text: Delayed care that has narrowed her options

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of her right to give informed consent

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced fertility because of the delay itself

explanation.summary: Financial, geographic, legal, and social barriers can delay abortion care and leave patients with fewer options.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that when abortion services are not locally available, access varies with financial, geographic, legal, and social factors, and individuals facing greater barriers may experience delays in obtaining care or have fewer available options. At 13 weeks she is beyond the US window for medical abortion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Abortion itself is not linked to increased long-term depression, and delay does not create that risk.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Misoprostol fever is a drug effect unrelated to access barriers.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Barriers to access do not remove a patient's capacity or right to consent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The lecture does not link delayed access to impaired fertility.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A fully trained physician performs a surgical abortion in a room without sterilization equipment, running water, or emergency supplies. The patient has no complications. According to the WHO definition, this abortion is best classified as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Safe, because a WHO-recommended method was used

choices.label: B
choices.text: Safe, because the provider had the necessary skills

choices.label: C
choices.text: Unsafe, because surgical methods carry higher risk

choices.label: D
choices.text: Unsafe, because the setting lacked basic standards

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unsafe, but only if a complication later develops

explanation.summary: WHO defines unsafe abortion as one performed by a person lacking the necessary skills, in an environment not meeting minimal medical standards, or both.
explanation.whyCorrect: WHO defines unsafe abortion as termination performed by a person lacking the necessary skills or in an environment not in conformity with minimal medical standards, or both. Either criterion alone makes an abortion unsafe, so a skilled provider working in a substandard setting still performs an unsafe abortion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An appropriate method does not offset a substandard environment.
whyWrongByChoice.B: WHO requires both a skilled provider and an environment meeting minimal medical standards.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Surgical abortion is a recommended safe method when properly performed.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Classification depends on the provider and setting, not on whether a complication occurs.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: According to WHO, approximately what proportion of patients who undergo an unsafe abortion are likely to develop temporary or lifelong physical and emotional health problems?

explanation.summary: As many as 25% of patients who undergo unsafe abortion develop temporary or lifelong physical and emotional health problems.
explanation.whyCorrect: WHO data in the lecture show that from 2010-2014, one in four pregnancies ended in abortion and about 25 million abortions were unsafe. Serious complications include hemorrhage, sepsis, peritonitis, and trauma to pelvic and abdominal organs, and as many as 25% of patients develop temporary or lifelong physical and emotional problems.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This underestimates the burden; WHO cites as many as 25%.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The lecture's WHO figure is as many as one in four patients.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This overstates the WHO estimate of up to 25%.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This greatly overstates the WHO estimate of up to 25%.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the timing and management of most abortions performed worldwide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: First trimester, mostly by dilation and evacuation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Second trimester, mostly by vacuum aspiration

explanation.summary: About 85%-90% of abortions worldwide occur in the first trimester (up to 12 weeks), and most are medically managed.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that most abortions worldwide (85%-90%) are performed in the first trimester, up to 12 weeks, with the majority medically managed. The method chosen generally depends on gestational age.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Most first-trimester abortions are medical; D&E is used later in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Most abortions occur in the first trimester and are medically managed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: 85%-90% of abortions occur in the first trimester, not the second.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Third-trimester abortions are uncommon and illegal in many countries.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman in the United States is at 11 weeks' gestation and prefers a medical rather than surgical abortion. Which of the following statements about medical abortion at her gestational age is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It exceeds both FDA-approved timing and WHO limits

choices.label: B
choices.text: It exceeds FDA-approved timing but is within WHO limits

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is FDA-approved through 12 weeks with mifepristone alone

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is FDA-approved through 14 weeks with misoprostol alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is within both FDA-approved timing and WHO limits

explanation.summary: In the US, medical abortion is FDA-approved to 10 weeks, whereas WHO considers it safe up to 12 weeks.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that in the US, medical abortions can be done up to 10 weeks according to FDA approval of the medications, but can be done safely up to 12 weeks according to WHO. At 11 weeks she falls between these limits.

whyWrongByChoice.A: WHO considers medical abortion safe up to 12 weeks, which includes 11 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mifepristone is used with misoprostol, and FDA approval runs to 10 weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Misoprostol alone is listed up to 10 weeks; 14 weeks is the vacuum aspiration limit.
whyWrongByChoice.E: FDA approval of the medications extends only to 10 weeks.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman at 12 weeks' gestation prefers a surgical abortion in the outpatient clinic. Which of the following is the most commonly used surgical method in the first trimester, and up to approximately what gestational age can it be used?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dilation and evacuation, up to about 10 weeks

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dilation and evacuation, up to about 14 weeks

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hysterotomy evacuation, up to about 12 weeks

choices.label: D
choices.text: Manual vacuum aspiration, up to about 14 weeks

choices.label: E
choices.text: Manual vacuum aspiration, up to about 24 weeks

explanation.summary: Manual vacuum aspiration is the most common first-trimester surgical method and can be used up to about 14 weeks.
explanation.whyCorrect: Manual vacuum aspiration uses gentle suctioning of the uterus to remove tissue and is used up to 10-14 weeks, making it the common first-trimester surgical method. Dilation and evacuation, which adds cervical dilation and instruments, is used up to 24 weeks.

whyWrongByChoice.A: D&E is used up to 24 weeks and is not the usual first-trimester surgical method.
whyWrongByChoice.B: D&E extends to 24 weeks; vacuum aspiration is the common first-trimester method.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hysterotomy is not among the lecture's surgical abortion methods.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 24 weeks is the upper limit for dilation and evacuation, not vacuum aspiration.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: Third-trimester abortions are uncommon and illegal in many countries, although some allow them in specific cases such as a threat to the patient's life, congenital anomalies, or domestic abuse. Which of the following is the main reason for these restrictions?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Certain mental illness after late abortion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inability to obtain informed consent late

choices.label: E
choices.text: Lack of any available surgical technique

explanation.summary: Third-trimester abortion is restricted in many countries mainly because of ethical concerns about fetal viability.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that third-trimester abortions are uncommon and illegal in many countries because of ethical concerns about fetal viability, but may be allowed in some countries when the patient's life or physical or mental health is in jeopardy, fetal congenital anomalies are present, or the patient is subject to domestic abuse.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibiotic prophylaxis is available for surgical abortion and is not the basis for restriction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Abortion is not associated with increased long-term mental health disorders.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Patients can give informed consent at any gestational age.
whyWrongByChoice.E: D&E and other techniques exist; restrictions are ethical, not technical.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A patient using a two-drug medical abortion regimen takes misoprostol as the second drug. Which of the following is the primary action by which misoprostol completes the abortion?

explanation.summary: Misoprostol causes uterine contractions that expel the conceptus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Per the lecture, misoprostol causes uterine contractions, expelling the conceptus. It is used up to 10 weeks with mifepristone, or alone when mifepristone is not available. Mifepristone's role is to block the progesterone that supports the pregnancy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Progesterone blockade is the mechanism of mifepristone, the first drug.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An antifolate action is not the mechanism of misoprostol.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Misoprostol contracts, rather than relaxes, the uterus to expel the conceptus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Misoprostol does not work through ovarian hormone suppression.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman is scheduled for manual vacuum aspiration at 9 weeks' gestation. In addition to sterile procedure protocol, which of the following is a recommended prophylactic agent before the procedure?

explanation.summary: ACOG and WHO recommend antibiotic prophylaxis for surgical abortion, using doxycycline, azithromycin, or metronidazole.
explanation.whyCorrect: For surgical abortion, ACOG and WHO recommend antibiotic prophylaxis in addition to sterile procedure protocol, which may be done with doxycycline, azithromycin, or metronidazole. With prophylaxis, post-procedure infection is uncommon (<1%).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acyclovir is an antiviral and is not used for abortion prophylaxis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fluconazole is an antifungal and is not an abortion prophylaxis agent.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nitrofurantoin is a urinary agent and is not among the recommended options.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oral vancomycin is not among the recommended prophylactic antibiotics.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman at 8 weeks' gestation is anxious before her manual vacuum aspiration. Which of the following pain management regimens is most frequently used for this procedure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acetaminophen alone after the procedure ends

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ibuprofen, diazepam, and a paracervical block

explanation.summary: Manual vacuum aspiration is usually managed with an NSAID, an anxiolytic/sedative, and a paracervical block.
explanation.whyCorrect: For manual vacuum aspiration, the most frequently used medications are NSAIDs such as ibuprofen and anxiolytics/sedatives such as diazepam, along with a paracervical block (local anesthetic injected into the cervix). Anxiety and fear can increase pain sensitivity, making the anxiolytic useful.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The usual regimen combines an NSAID, an anxiolytic, and local anesthesia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: General anesthesia is reserved for D&E at more advanced gestational ages.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Opioids are added after the procedure only if NSAIDs fail to control pain.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neuraxial anesthesia is not described for vacuum aspiration.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 19-year-old woman has heavy bleeding 3 days after a medical abortion at 7 weeks' gestation. Ultrasound shows no retained products of conception. She reports heavy menses and frequent nosebleeds since menarche. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in evaluation?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Speculum repair of a cervical laceration

explanation.summary: Hemorrhage after medical abortion warrants evaluation for retained products and for an underlying bleeding disorder.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that hemorrhage after medical abortion should prompt evaluation for incomplete abortion (retained products of conception) as well as possible evaluation for an underlying bleeding disorder. With retained tissue excluded and a history of lifelong bleeding symptoms, coagulation testing is the next step.

whyWrongByChoice.A: She has no fever, pain, or discharge to suggest infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Perforation is a complication of surgical abortion, which she did not have.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ultrasound has excluded retained products, so there is nothing to evacuate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cervical trauma is a cause of bleeding after surgical, not medical, abortion.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman is scheduled for dilation and evacuation at 16 weeks' gestation. Which of the following is the typical approach to anesthesia for this procedure?

choices.label: B
choices.text: No analgesia or sedation is typically given

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oral diazepam alone before the procedure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral ibuprofen alone before the procedure

explanation.summary: D&E is typically performed under IV sedation, with general anesthesia used at more advanced gestational ages.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that dilation and evacuation is typically performed under IV sedation (conscious or deep intravenous sedation), while procedures at more advanced gestational ages are performed under general anesthesia. If NSAIDs do not control pain afterward, oral, IM, or IV opioids can be given.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Pain is the most common complication, and D&E requires sedation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An oral anxiolytic alone is insufficient; D&E typically uses IV sedation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: NSAIDs alone are used for medical abortion cramps, not for D&E.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A paracervical block is part of vacuum aspiration analgesia; D&E is typically done under IV sedation.

questions.topicName: Abortion Care: Safety, Management, and Outcomes

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman at 6 weeks' gestation calls several hours after taking misoprostol for a medical abortion. She reports strong cramping abdominal pain but has no fever and only moderate bleeding. Which of the following is the most appropriate management of her pain?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A paracervical block at the bedside

choices.label: C
choices.text: An NSAID such as ibuprofen as needed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immediate vacuum aspiration for the pain

explanation.summary: Cramps during medical abortion are usually self-limited and treated with NSAIDs as needed.
